## 開篇固定收益論點

美國公債週二延續9月以來的跌勢，但與其說市場遭遇新的政策衝擊，不如說在油價逼近$110、聯準會準備升息且公共部門融資成本持續攀升之際，投資人再次衡量自己願意承接多少長天期利率風險。10年期殖利率盤中升至5.04%，為2007年以來最高，終場上升1.5個基點至5.003%；30年期上升2.2個基點至5.368%，2年期與5年期則僅分別上升0.4與0.6個基點，至4.664%與4.829%。

這樣的漲幅分布使殖利率曲線當日小幅陡峭化，不同於本輪賣壓較早階段由政策預期主導的明顯平坦化。2年與10年期利差擴大1.1個基點至33.9個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大1.8個基點至70.4個基點。不過，過去一週2年期與10年期殖利率已分別上升26.9與21.3個基點，整體走勢仍反映市場大幅重估聯準會的預期利率路徑。週二新增的壓力主要落在殖利率曲線較長端，投資人一方面面對油價再度上漲，另一方面消化$130億的20年期公債標售；本次得標殖利率為5.420%，高於前次的5.204%。

從通膨定價的分解來看，當日名目殖利率升幅主要來自實質殖利率。10年期實質殖利率上升1.3個基點至2.62%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則僅上升0.2個基點至2.383%。油價仍是最顯眼的通膨風險：沙烏地阿拉伯東西輸油管停擺，加上利比亞油田生產受阻，威脅原油供給，WTI上漲3.93%至$105.37，布蘭特原油上漲2.48%至$108.30。然而，損益兩平通膨率反應有限，顯示美債市場認為緊縮政策、龐大融資需求，以及持有長天期債券所要求的實質補償，比長期通膨預期失控更能解釋目前的定價。

美國數據好壞不一。ADP每週估計顯示，私人就業增加16,250人，高於修正後的12,250人。9月紐約州製造業指數則由20.60降至7.60，低於14.75的市場共識，顯示區域製造業活動雖仍擴張，放緩程度卻遠超預期。兩項數據並未動搖市場對聯準會升息1碼的預期：會議日期交換利率顯示，聯準會將目前3.5%-3.75%的目標區間上調1碼的機率約為94%，年底前則已反映約50個基點的緊縮幅度。

風險資產走弱，但未出現全面性的融資壓力。標普500指數下跌0.45%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.65%，VIX則微升至17.2。美元指數上漲0.15%；實質殖利率走高的影響超過地緣政治對黃金的支撐，黃金期貨下跌0.58%至$4,326.50。美國投資級債利差小幅收窄，高收益債利差則小幅擴大；LQD幾乎持平，HYG與JNK分別下跌約0.19%與0.20%。新興市場債也走弱，EMB下跌約0.25%，一項開發中國家貨幣指數連續第4個交易日下跌。

在另有國內供給或財政因素的市場，全球利率上行壓力更為劇烈。市場傳出日本政府考慮將國防支出目標提高至GDP的3.5%，使日本10年期公債殖利率升至3.03%，創1996年以來最高。印度市場在假期後恢復交易，投資人消化央行出售債券、收回過剩流動性的計畫，5年期公債殖利率一度上升22個基點。中國則走向相反方向：數據顯示出口支撐的工業生產，與格外疲弱的家庭支出、房地產投資及資本形成之間差距擴大，但政府公債殖利率變動不大。

## 美國公債守在5%以上，供給風險移向長端

10年期美債收在5%以上，其意義大於當日相對有限的漲幅。前一個交易日殖利率曾短暫突破這道門檻，但收盤仍略低於5%；週二則先升至5.04%，再回落至5.003%。這顯示近20年最高殖利率附近仍有買盤進場，但力道尚不足以讓指標殖利率明確回到5%以下。

$130億的20年期公債增額發行，進一步測試投資人對流動性較低、利率敏感度較高券種的承接意願。標售得標殖利率為5.420%，高於前次的5.204%，也高於標售前交易時約5.40%的殖利率，創該年期2020年恢復發行以來最高。標售後長天期美債跌勢擴大，但現有結果未提供投標倍數、投資人獲配比重或正式的發行前交易比較，因此無法計算標售尾差。

即便如此，較高的得標殖利率仍清楚顯示政府融資成本正在上升。此時，美國公債供給還須與企業發債及人工智慧相關資本支出競爭資金。結構性問題並非標售已完全失去買方，而是政府需要為到期債務再融資、財政赤字居高不下，且央行不再透過量化寬鬆吸收供給之際，對價格愈來愈敏感的投資人要求更高補償。

週二實質殖利率的變化正反映這項壓力。10年期實質殖利率升至2.62%，較一週前上升20.5個基點、較一個月前上升21個基點；相較之下，10年期損益兩平通膨率一週僅上升0.8個基點，雖然一個月累計升幅達10個基點。這項差異關係到賣壓如何傳導：即使市場隱含的通膨補償仍相對受控，實質折現率上升也會透過房貸、企業債與股票全面收緊金融情勢。

油價衝擊持續升高，也加大必須進一步收緊政策才能遏制通膨的風險。布蘭特原油一週上漲近10.6%，收在$108附近；WTI同期漲幅超過13.2%。沙烏地阿拉伯東西輸油管在遭到攻擊後仍未恢復運作；該管線通往紅海，可繞過荷莫茲海峽。沙烏地阿美延後向部分歐洲客戶交貨，利比亞供應中斷又增添另一項干擾。儘管價格上漲本身可能削弱需求，這些因素仍持續推高原油與成品油價格。

固定收益市場收盤時，美國石油協會公布的估計為國內市場提供了一項潛在緩衝。截至9月11日的一週，美國原油庫存增加714萬桶，市場原先預期減少180萬桶，前一週則減少30萬桶。這項估計無法化解海外供應限制，能源資訊署的官方數據仍是更完整的檢驗依據；不過，如此大幅的庫存增加，可以降低市場對原油各環節都同樣日益短缺的判斷。

當日總體數據也顯示，不宜把美債走勢單純視為經濟成長加速的結果。ADP每週就業估計增加4,000人至16,250人，支持私人勞動需求仍在擴張的看法。另一方面，紐約州製造業指數大跌13點至7.60，低於14.75的市場共識與14的預測值。指數仍高於零，但這波下滑削弱了製造業動能在聯準會會議前增強的論點。

截至9月12日的一週，Redbook同店銷售年增8.5%，高於前一週的8.3%，顯示部分零售商的名目支出仍強。這項指標涵蓋範圍小於政府零售銷售報告，也未區分銷售量與價格，因此只能補充當期美元計價消費仍有支撐的證據，無法判斷家庭究竟買了更多商品，還是為同樣的商品支付更高價格。

6週期國庫券標售得標殖利率為3.850%，高於前次的3.740%，符合政策利率預期上升的方向。不過，由於缺乏投標倍數與獲配資訊，結果不足以判定需求強弱；國庫券的走勢也不具融資壓力特徵，沒有理由將其解讀為與附息公債殖利率曲線相互矛盾。

即使政策結果本身符合預期，偏空部位也提高了聯準會決策引發劇烈行情的可能性。摩根大通美債客戶調查顯示，截至9月14日的一週，空頭部位比重增加10個百分點，創2025年初以來最快增幅，中性部位則減少8個百分點。期貨未平倉部位也顯示，投資人在高於預期的通膨報告公布前後都增加了看空部位。美國銀行指出，空頭部位廣泛分布於整條殖利率曲線，幾乎看不到資產管理機構逢低承接。

這種偏空程度具有重要的短線意義，因為它可能放大雙向波動。若聯準會訊息暗示年底前的緊縮幅度將超過市場已反映的約50個基點，現有空頭部位便會獲得支持。反之，若聯準會如充分預告般升息1碼，並提供可信但有限的後續指引，則可能促使投資人獲利了結，尤其10年期殖利率已接近5%，部位也相當極端。

市場對維持利率不變的準備遠為不足。交換利率已反映週三升息約23個基點，接近完整的1碼。自2008年以來，只要預期達到這種程度，聯準會最終都會升息。德意志銀行估計，若利率不變，將是聯準會自1994年開始在會議後立即宣布決策以來，例行會議中幅度最大的鴿派意外。暫停升息可能壓低對政策較敏感的短端殖利率；但若投資人因此認為決策官員容忍過多通膨風險，長端殖利率反而可能上升。

股票同時承受折現率與能源價格壓力。標普500成分股中超過350檔下跌，道瓊指數跌約1%；整體標普500與Nasdaq跌幅較小，費城半導體指數則在前一週大幅走弱後上漲0.40%。因此，股市跌勢雖廣泛，並非不分標的一概拋售。美債殖利率上升降低了遠期現金流的現值，油價上漲則直接提高消費者與企業利潤率面對的成本。

比特幣更鮮明地反映風險敏感度。美國參議院未能推進《Clarity Act》，法案需取得60票，表決結果卻為49票贊成、50票反對；比特幣隨後一度下跌5.3%至$74,910。以太幣盤中跌逾8%，表決前最後一小時內，近$3億的加密貨幣多頭部位遭到清算。立法受挫是直接催化因素，但市場對利率上升與流動性收緊的憂慮也加劇了跌勢。

## 日本與印度的國內供給衝擊加劇全球債市賣壓

日本債市下跌既反映全球殖利率上升，也加入新的國內財政疑問。市場傳出政府考慮將中期國防支出目標提高至GDP的3.5%，帶動10年期日本公債殖利率上升4.5個基點至3.03%，創1996年以來最高。政府也在考慮較低的3%目標，目前尚未作出正式承諾。

相較日本近期預算，潛在調升幅度相當可觀。高市早苗政府已加速提高國防相關支出，在截至3月的會計年度接近GDP的2%，較原訂時程提前兩年完成。不過，依日本內閣府的名目GDP預測，本會計年度國防及相關支出為¥10.6兆，實際僅約占GDP的1.5%；按此基礎計算，若提高至3.5%，支出將約達¥24兆，超過目前金額的兩倍。

資金來源仍未確定。國防省為明年4月開始的會計年度提出創紀錄的¥8.9兆預算要求，較本年度增加0.9%，但其中許多項目尚未編列具體成本。新的五年國防計畫預計在年底前公布。日本官員已向美方表示願意增加支出，公開立場則仍是應由軍事需求決定所需經費，而非預先設定一個金額目標。

這項消息蓋過了20年期日本公債標售的正面結果。投標倍數為4.01，高於前次的3.98與過去12個月平均的3.73；標售尾差由0.17縮小至0.15，買盤也來自多家國內金融機構。這些結果顯示，投資人願意按標售殖利率承接日本長天期公債，卻無法解答擴大國防支出最終需要增加多少債務的問題。

日本央行週五的決策，也讓投資人更有理由控制長天期部位。市場普遍預期升息，因此總裁植田和男對後續緊縮速度與幅度的指引，才是更大的變數。較高政策利率、日圓疲弱與可能擴張的財政支出都對日本公債殖利率形成同方向壓力，儘管可信的緊縮路徑最終可能約束通膨預期。

印度的賣壓則更直接來自一項已知的資產負債表操作真正進入市場。週一假期結束後，5年期政府公債殖利率一度跳升22個基點，為2022年5月以來最大漲幅；指標10年期殖利率則上升8個基點。短天期券種承壓特別明顯，是因印度央行計畫出售1兆盧比債券，其中多數為3至6年到期的證券。

印度央行希望收回其視為通膨風險的過剩資金。直接賣出債券比暫時性的附賣回操作更能持久抽走流動性，但也會增加市場可交易供給；未來6個月，印度市場本已須承接接近8兆盧比的中央政府借款，各邦政府發債通常也相當龐大。央行仍有繼續操作的能力：上一個會計年度，其主權債持有量增加逾40%至約23兆盧比，相當於中央政府流通在外證券約18%。

油價又進一步加重壓力。印度大部分原油仰賴進口，因此油價高於$100會同時惡化通膨、經常帳與能源相關財政負擔。8月通膨已更接近印度央行2%-6%目標區間的上緣。Kotak Mahindra經濟學家Upasna Bhardwaj預期利率將上調50至75個基點，並認為10月升息的可能性已明顯提高。

債市恢復交易時，盧比走弱，印度央行也進場支撐匯率，但干預並未消除政策取捨。出售美元可以減輕匯率壓力，卻也會收回盧比流動性；出售債券則更直接抽走資金，同時使殖利率曲線短端與中段面對額外供給。由此產生的曲線平坦化，不同於美國市場當日的小幅陡峭化，因為印度央行的操作直接鎖定3至6年期券種。

## 中國工業韌性未能傳導至內需

中國8月數據顯示，經濟愈來愈依賴工業生產與出口，消費、投資及房地產則持續疲弱。零售銷售年增率僅0.4%，低於0.8%的市場共識，也慢於7月的0.6%。今年前8個月固定資產投資較去年同期下滑7.2%，略差於預期；房地產投資則萎縮19.9%。

勞動市場也轉弱，城鎮失業率意外由5.2%升至5.3%。取消購車補貼抑制需求，汽車銷售較去年同期下跌18.5%；不含汽車的零售銷售成長2.5%，與7月相同。這顯示消費疲弱並非遍及所有類別，但在重要的非必需消費項目中仍十分嚴重。

工業生產是主要支撐。產出年增5.2%，高於預期，也較7月的4.5%加速。全球人工智慧基礎設施建置帶動的出口需求，支撐積體電路與其他高科技產品。在政府「六網」計畫推進之下，1至8月資訊傳輸領域的資本支出成長28.4%，高於前7個月的26%。

外部生產與國內所得的落差因而更加鮮明。強勁出口可以支撐整體經濟成長率，卻尚未帶來足夠的家庭信心或企業投資以振興內需。製造業7月平均利潤率為4.9%，雖優於一年前，仍低於2021年的6.7%。房地產價值下跌及就業市場惡化繼續限制消費。

巴克萊、Oxford Economics與麥格理根據7、8月數據估計，第3季GDP年增率約為4.3%。這將使經濟成長可能連續第2季低於官方4.5%-5%的目標區間。風險在於，即使國內需求惡化，出口強勢仍可能使政策制定者延後推出更廣泛的逆景氣支持。

市場對政策的期待仍較克制。近期較可能的回應，是加快動用已核准的預算額度，而非推出大型新刺激方案。政府擬改革房地產預售制度、降低開發商對該模式的依賴，或可保護購屋者；但若開發商取得房貸款項的時間延後，也可能進一步削弱建設意願，並拖累地方政府財政。

中國市場把這批數據視為既有低成長環境的再次確認，而不是新的即時政策衝擊。在岸與離岸人民幣匯率均持穩，10年期政府公債殖利率也大致持平於1.68%。這份穩定與美國、日本及印度債市的賣壓形成對比，也有助於解釋能以低成本取得本幣融資的亞洲高收益發行人為何表現相對較強。

## 信用市場仍暢通，個別發行人壓力更為明顯

儘管美債殖利率上升，美國整體信用市場仍有秩序。投資級債利差小幅收窄，高收益債利差也僅小幅擴大。LQD總報酬幾乎持平，HYG與JNK則各下跌約0.20%；這項差異顯示市場仍在區分長天期利率壓力與較低品質債券新增的信用風險，而非陷入全面性拋售。

底層融資格局則較為複雜。KKR表示，2026年上半年經其安排或聯貸的私人投資級交易超過$800億；截至9月1日，今年承作金額已達2025年全年的兩倍。許多交易由保險資金提供主要支撐，借款人也愈來愈常透過特殊目的載體，在資產負債表外為資產融資，以維持公司評等並取得投資資金。

人工智慧是這類需求的重要來源。KKR估計，未來五年AI基礎設施可能需要$7.6兆的資本支出，規模很可能超過傳統資產負債表與公開債券市場所能單獨承擔的能力。該公司今年已募集$150億第三方信用資本，較2025年同期增加29%；在其管理的$2,930億整體信用資產中，私人信貸占$1,390億。

私人投資級融資的成長並未消除專案風險。凱雷集團的Jason Thomas警告，部分資料中心貸款高度仰賴發起人的投資級信用，而非獨立評估底層專案收入。他將這種結構比作金融危機前的一項假設：銀行必要時能夠承接房貸曝險。Thomas強調，目前投資級發起人的處境不同於當時的銀行；但隨著負債增加、資料中心營運結果的可能範圍擴大，這項支持最終仍可能轉弱。

隨著風險溢價收窄，授信審查問題更顯重要。如果貸款機構把發起人的資產負債表視為主要保障，承諾金額迅速擴張，就會使每一個新增專案更容易受到設施本身營運表現拖累。此外，租戶集中、電力供應、運算技術變化與AI收入實現時點，仍是較傳統的風險。

Brightshore Capital則進入另一個因高利率而產生私人信貸機會的領域。這家房地產管理公司推出規模$2.5億的債務平台，聚焦延伸優先順位貸款、夾層融資、特別股與B類債權。Brightshore表示，透過出售交易中的優先順位部分，這筆資本可支援超過$10億的交易。

住宅建商與開發商正同時面對建築成本居高不下、大量債務到期，以及遠高於專案啟動時的再融資利率。奧斯汀等供給過剩的市場尤其脆弱，因為租金下滑、營運成本上升，又碰上建築貸款到期。這項平台的推出顯示，私人資本正流向再融資缺口；然而，創造這些機會的相同條件，也提高了抵押品表現惡化的風險。

個別發行人的損失呈現這類機會的另一面。土耳其能源公司Zorlu Enerji聘請Houlihan Lokey與Servo Capital擔任債務顧問後，其2030年到期美元債一度重挫11點至面額約63美分，創歷來最大跌幅。Zorlu集團旗下另一家公司Vestel Elektronik兩個月前才聘請Houlihan參與重整協商，引發財務壓力正在集團內擴散的疑慮。

Zorlu Enerji上半年營收由一年前的173億里拉降至130億里拉。過去12個月里拉兌美元貶值約15%，提高其國際債務換算成本；年中淨負債則為$12.5億。公司在2024年首度發行$10億國際債券。由於顧問才剛獲聘，債券下跌反映的是市場對後續程序的不確定，而非各方已談妥重整條款。

Biscuit International完成債務管理交易僅三個月後，旗下貸款也進一步陷入困境。管理階層告知債權人，第2季與初夏營運疲弱，原因包括銷量下降，以及農產品與原料成本上升。原物料避險預計無法完全抵銷壓力，因市場競爭限制公司把成本轉嫁給客戶的能力。

6月交易延長了定期貸款與循環信用額度的期限，將€1.3億票據置於次順位，並修改一筆€1.5億第二順位貸款的付款條件。這些措施爭取了更多時間，但穆迪仍認為其資本結構無法持續，流動性也偏弱。公司營運資金需求高，若營業現金流持續惡化，僅延長期限仍不足以解決信用問題。

亞洲高收益債呈現不同的區域面貌。美元計價亞洲非投資級債今年報酬率為4.3%，高於美國同類債券的1.8%，其殖利率溢價並在前一週降至歷史最低。穆迪研究顯示，截至7月，其評等範圍內的美國企業有43家違約，歐洲、中東與非洲合計20家，亞太地區則僅1家。

中國較低廉的國內融資與亞洲較快的成長，支撐了發行人的基本面。即使評等較低的中國企業，也能以約1.7%的利率取得較短期限本幣融資。亞洲不含日本的非金融高收益美元債發行量較去年同期增加20%至約$120億，但仍遠低於美國逾$2,200億的高收益債發行規模。

這項領先表現也帶來估值風險。截至報導日，亞洲高收益債券9月下跌0.4%，中國非投資級債則上漲0.2%。聯準會升息與美債殖利率上升，可能迫使中國以外的亞洲央行收緊政策或捍衛匯率，進而提高當地融資成本。在中國房地產債券市場崩落後，區域發行量曾降至低檔，如今也開始回升；中國房地產債市場過去每年曾發行逾$500億高收益債券。

在整體新興市場走弱之際，加彭則是個別國家情勢改善凌駕大盤的例子。政府稽核把合併債務估計修正為$167億，較初估少近五分之一，相當於GDP的69%。2031年2月到期債券上漲1.36美分至每1美元面額87.84美分，使加彭三檔國際債券成為當日新興市場表現最佳的債券。

稽核檢視未執行專案、未進入國庫帳戶的資金及其他承諾後，把2025年底認列的債務總額由近11.7兆非洲金融共同體法郎降至9.5兆。政府已把結果提交國際貨幣基金，計畫用於新方案、積欠款項清償及永續債務策略的談判。較低債務總額改善了談判起點，但加彭仍須就已核實債務的償付方式達成協議，並防止出現新的積欠款項。

印尼主權信用的改善則較有保留。總統普拉伯沃以市場熟悉的前財政部副部長Suahasil Nazara，取代財政部長Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa。此次任命接續印尼央行領導層更替，被視為政府試圖穩定制度；此前政策反覆已導致今年約$19億資金外流。

Nazara承諾維持審慎政策，並把赤字控制在GDP 3%的法定上限以下。投資人仍希望看到他在為總統社會計畫與成長方案籌資、釐清主權財富基金Danantara角色的同時，能否維持財政紀律。印尼本地債券已連續四個月獲得外資流入，盧比也自6月低點回升約3%；但週二匯率下跌顯示，人事變動並未消除市場對油價與全球利率的敏感度。

## 歐洲利率定價走在央行指引之前

歐洲貨幣市場反映的能源衝擊因應路徑，持續比央行官員的指引更為積極。交換利率顯示，未來12個月歐洲央行還將升息4次、每次1碼，英格蘭銀行則將升息5次。天然氣價格已回到2022年所見水準，油價突破$108，推升短天期殖利率與預期利率波動。

自伊朗衝突開始以來，歐洲央行已兩度升息，最近一次將存款利率提高至中性利率估計區間的上緣。官員不願承諾固定的升息路徑。總裁拉加德承認，由於能源衝擊持續時間超出預期，通膨將維持高檔；但市場目前反映的路徑，會把政策利率推入明顯限制性區域。

英格蘭銀行與市場之間的溝通落差更大。副總裁Dave Ramsden先前表示，他對目前政策感到放心，但也承認存在上行風險。市場預期週四會議不會調整利率，交換市場卻仍給予立即升息30%的機率。決策後不會舉行記者會，因此聲明文字必須同時回應通膨衝擊，以及市場預期的5次升息。

資產負債表政策可能另行調整。據報英格蘭銀行、英國財政部與債務管理辦公室官員已擬定計畫，可能停止主動出售長天期英國公債，但貨幣政策委員會尚未作成最終決定。市場預期自10月起，年度資產負債表縮減規模將降至£500億。若按此速度維持現有出售組合，主動出售長天期公債的金額將僅約£40億；這是因為目前計畫中，期限長於中期區段的到期債券約占20%。

停止主動出售可減少一項未來長天期債券供給，卻不等於逆轉量化緊縮。在30年期英國公債殖利率接近5.9%，而央行因金融危機與疫情後購入的債券承受龐大損失之際，這項差異格外重要。政策調整處理的是市場承接能力，不能取代利率決策。

法國官員試圖向投資人保證，殖利率上升並未妨礙政府取得融資。財政部長Roland Lescure表示，國庫已完成全年發債計畫的85%；法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin則表示，投標金額持續高於發售規模。即便如此，法國10年期公債相對德國的利差仍在約97個基點交易，此前更一度升至歐元區債務危機以來未見水準。

這項壓力並非僅來自全球債市賣壓。法國面對龐大赤字、成長疲弱，以及七個月後的總統大選；能源成本提高與全球發債量增加，又加重國內風險。Moulin認為央行公信力至關重要，因為殖利率上升有一部分來自通膨預期；他同時指出，美國科技業借款也加劇了全球資本競爭。

投資人愈來愈重視歐洲各主權發行人的差異，不再一概把核心國家視為更安全。儘管保加利亞公共債務僅約占GDP的30%，其10年期公債殖利率仍為4.40%，比德國高近90個基點。拉脫維亞與立陶宛是今年表現最佳的歐元計價主權債市場，法國與比利時則下跌約3%。

匈牙利大選結束Viktor Orban長達16年的執政後，新政府提出2030年採用歐元的目標，也吸引資金流入。該計畫包括把預估達7.5%的財政赤字降至GDP的3%；外資持有的匈牙利公債與國庫券在7月創下新高。投資機會仍伴隨匯率、流動性與能源風險，但在區域指標殖利率普遍上升時，這項轉變顯示財政方向的重要性可能高於傳統地理分類。

## 前瞻市場意義

聯準會9月16日的利率決策、經濟預測，以及主席Kevin Warsh的記者會，是美債市場的核心考驗；目前部位已大幅偏向殖利率上升。聯邦基金利率目標區間現為3.5%-3.75%，市場幾乎一致預期升息1碼。眼前問題不只是聯準會是否照預期行動，也包括經濟預測與Warsh的說法，是否支持市場已反映的年底前約50個基點緊縮幅度。

維持利率不變會是更大的意外，並可能使殖利率曲線兩端分化：短端殖利率可能失去部分預期政策溢價；如果投資人質疑聯準會對通膨的反應，長端殖利率則可能上升。升息1碼但搭配異常耐心的指引，也會帶來程度較輕的同類風險。若聯準會對後續行動釋出強硬訊息，將支持短端重新定價，卻也可能推高實質殖利率，加深股票、住宅與利率敏感型信用債面對的壓力。

週二數據讓辯論雙方都有依據。ADP每週就業估計改善至16,250人，紐約州製造業指數卻降至7.60，遠低於市場共識。聯準會必須權衡仍有韌性的聘僱與名目支出，以及製造業動能放緩的跡象。

8月零售銷售及進出口價格將在政策公布前出爐。整體零售銷售預期在前月下跌0.6%後上升0.8%；進口價格預期在下跌0.4%後上升0.4%，出口價格則預期在下跌1.3%後上升0.5%。這些數據將顯示，外部成本壓力上升之際，家庭需求是否同步回升。紐約聯準銀行服務業指數、企業庫存與NAHB房市指數，則將提供範圍較窄的經濟活動及利率敏感度訊號。

油價仍可能改變市場對數據的解讀。EIA官方庫存報告將接續API估計的原油庫存增加714萬桶；若官方數據也顯示類似的大幅增加，可為國內市場提供部分緩衝，抵銷國際供應衝擊。更關鍵的實體市場問題，是沙烏地阿拉伯能否恢復東西輸油管、延後運往歐洲的貨物能否交付，以及利比亞產量能否回升。若中東出口能力長期受損，美國庫存累積也無法完全抵銷影響。

9月17日公布的勞動市場與區域製造業數據，將檢驗紐約州製造業指數下滑是否屬於孤立現象。初領失業救濟人數預期由206,000人升至208,000人，續領人數預期由177.4萬人升至178萬人。費城聯準銀行製造業指數預期由47.4降至30.5；其中就業、新訂單、資本支出與支付價格分項，將顯示經濟活動是全面放緩，還是在成本壓力持續之際仍維持強勁。

美國財政部9月17日將標售10年期TIPS，前次得標殖利率為2.438%。目前市場10年期實質殖利率已達2.62%，一週上升逾20個基點。在名目20年期公債以較高殖利率完成標售，且整體美債市場以10年期殖利率高於5%收盤後，這次標售將測試投資人對通膨保值長天期債券的需求。

英格蘭銀行9月17日的決策包含兩個彼此獨立的層面。市場預期政策利率維持不變，但能源價格上升使升息仍有相當機率；政策聲明也必須說明下一年度的量化緊縮計畫。若確認放慢資產負債表縮減，並停止主動出售長天期英國公債，可減少殖利率曲線最長端的供給壓力，但無法解決通膨問題。

日本央行將於9月18日接續公布決策。市場普遍預期升息，因此植田和男的指引將比這次升息本身提供更多市場資訊。若釋出持續緊縮的訊號，可支撐日圓，卻可能使日本公債殖利率維持高檔，並鼓勵日本機構把更多資金留在國內。尚未定案的國防支出提案則構成另一項財政考驗；投資人必須知道最終目標、執行期間與資金來源，才能判斷需要增加多少發債。

印度下一項考驗是央行實際執行債券出售計畫。首批操作將集中在殖利率曲線短端與中段券種。週二5年期殖利率上升22個基點，已顯示該區段對直接收回流動性有多敏感。標售截止利率與盧比走勢，將顯示調整是否仍局限於特定年期，或演變為更廣泛的金融情勢收緊。

市場將持續關注中國至9月底的政策反應。工業生產仍足夠強勁，使決策官員缺乏立即推出大型刺激措施的誘因；但零售銷售僅成長0.4%、投資萎縮7.2%，房地產投資下跌19.9%，都在提高延後行動的成本。加快動用既有財政額度可以支撐基礎建設與生產；若要採取更廣泛的對策，則需看到官員願意處理家庭所得與房地產疲弱，而非主要依靠出口。

信用市場面對的是各項交易能否落實，而非單一整體指標的考驗。Zorlu Enerji的顧問必須釐清工作範圍究竟是再融資、出售資產，還是更廣泛的重整。Biscuit International則必須證明，6月延長債務期限後，仍能承受營運持續疲弱與營運資金壓力。隨著負債增加，為AI與房地產提供資金的私人貸款機構，也將以發起人支持與抵押品現金流是否仍可信來接受檢驗。

加彭修正後的債務總額，必須轉化為與IMF及其他金融夥伴之間的協議。稽核改善了獲認列的資產負債表狀況，並立即帶動債券上漲；但下一階段仍需制定已核實積欠款項與未來借款的處理方案。印尼的Nazara也將透過2027年預算面對類似的公信力考驗：若能在為政府政策議程提供資金的同時，把赤字維持在GDP的3%以下，將比單純更換內閣提供更有力的證據。

綜觀這些事件，市場面對的並非資本消失。美國公債標售、私人投資級交易及部分新興市場信用債，仍能吸引買方。眼前真正的限制是價格：政府與企業依然可以借款，但在油價上漲、貨幣緊縮及長期融資需求相互競爭之際，市場要求的實質殖利率、契約保障與發起人支持都在提高。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their September decline on Tuesday, but the session was less a fresh policy shock than another test of how much long-duration risk investors would absorb with oil near $110, the Federal Reserve poised to raise rates and public borrowing costs still climbing. The 10-year yield ended at 5.003%, up 1.5 basis points after reaching 5.04% intraday, its highest level since 2007. The 30-year rose 2.2 basis points to 5.368%, while the 2-year and 5-year yields increased only 0.4 and 0.6 basis point, to 4.664% and 4.829%.

That distribution produced a modest daily steepening rather than the pronounced policy-led flattening seen earlier in the selloff. The 2s10s spread widened 1.1 basis points to 33.9 and 2s30s widened 1.8 basis points to 70.4. Over the past week, however, the 2-year yield has risen 26.9 basis points and the 10-year 21.3 basis points, leaving the broader move consistent with a substantial repricing of the expected Fed path. Tuesday’s marginal pressure was concentrated further out the curve as investors confronted another oil advance and a $13 billion 20-year auction that cleared at 5.420%, up from 5.204% at the previous sale.

The inflation decomposition showed that the day’s nominal increase came principally through real yields. The 10-year real yield rose 1.3 basis points to 2.62%, while the 10-year breakeven increased only 0.2 basis point to 2.383%. Oil was still the most visible inflation risk: WTI gained 3.93% to $105.37 and Brent rose 2.48% to $108.30 as the outage of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and disruptions at Libyan fields threatened supply. Yet the limited breakeven response suggested the Treasury market was assigning greater weight to tighter policy, heavy financing needs and the real compensation required to hold duration than to an uncontrolled rise in long-run inflation expectations.

U.S. data were mixed. ADP’s weekly estimate showed private employment increasing by 16,250, up from a revised 12,250. The September Empire State Manufacturing Index fell to 7.60 from 20.60, below the 14.75 consensus, indicating that regional factory activity remained positive but slowed much more than expected. The combination did not dislodge expectations for a quarter-point Fed increase: meeting-dated swaps assigned about a 94% probability to a move from the current 3.5%-3.75% target range, with roughly 50 basis points of tightening priced through year-end.

Risk assets weakened without showing generalized funding stress. The S&P 500 fell 0.45% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.65%, while the VIX edged up to 17.2. The Dollar Index gained 0.15%, and gold futures declined 0.58% to $4,326.50 as higher real yields outweighed the metal’s geopolitical support. U.S. investment-grade spreads tightened modestly, while high-yield spreads widened modestly; the LQD fund was nearly unchanged, whereas HYG and JNK lost about 0.19% and 0.20%. Emerging-market debt also weakened, with EMB down roughly 0.25% and a developing-nation currency index falling for a fourth session.

The global rate pressure was more severe in markets facing their own supply or fiscal catalysts. Japan’s 10-year yield reached 3.03%, its highest since 1996, after reports that the government was considering a defense-spending goal as high as 3.5% of GDP. India’s 5-year yield rose as much as 22 basis points when local trading resumed after a holiday and investors absorbed the central bank’s plan to sell bonds to remove surplus liquidity. China moved in the other direction: government yields were little changed after data exposed a wider divide between export-supported industrial production and exceptionally weak household spending, property investment and capital formation.

## Treasuries Hold Above 5% as Supply Risk Moves to the Long End

The 10-year Treasury’s close above 5% carried more significance than its relatively small daily move. The yield had crossed the threshold briefly in the preceding session before finishing just below it. On Tuesday it reached 5.04%, then retreated to 5.003%, showing that buyers were still willing to enter at the highest yields in almost two decades but were not yet strong enough to return the benchmark decisively below 5%.

The 20-year auction tested that willingness in a less liquid and more duration-sensitive sector. The $13 billion reopening cleared at 5.420%, compared with 5.204% at the previous auction and a yield near 5.40% in pre-auction trading. The result was the highest auction yield since the tenor was reintroduced in 2020. Longer-dated Treasuries extended their declines after the sale, although the available result did not include the bid-to-cover ratio, investor allotments or a formal when-issued comparison from which to calculate a tail.

The higher award rate nevertheless documented the increase in the government’s funding cost. It also arrived as Treasury supply competes with corporate issuance and capital spending associated with artificial intelligence. The structural concern is not that auctions have lost all buyers, but that increasingly price-sensitive investors require greater compensation as governments refinance maturing debt, fiscal deficits remain large and central banks no longer absorb supply through quantitative easing.

That pressure was visible in the real-yield component of Tuesday’s move. At 2.62%, the 10-year real yield was 20.5 basis points higher than a week earlier and 21 basis points higher over the month. The 10-year breakeven, by contrast, had risen only 0.8 basis point over the week, though it was 10 basis points higher over the month. The distinction matters for the transmission of the selloff: a rise in real discount rates tightens financial conditions across mortgages, corporate debt and equities even if market-based inflation compensation remains comparatively contained.

The oil shock continued to raise the risk that containment will require more policy restraint. Brent settled near $108 after gaining almost 10.6% over the week, while WTI had risen more than 13.2%. Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, which provides a route to the Red Sea that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, remained offline after attacks. Saudi Aramco was delaying deliveries to some European customers, and Libyan outages added another source of disruption. The combination kept pressure on crude and refined products even though higher prices themselves threaten to weaken demand.

An American Petroleum Institute estimate released at the end of the fixed-income session offered a potential domestic counterweight. U.S. crude inventories increased by 7.14 million barrels in the week through Sept. 11, against expectations for a 1.8 million-barrel decline and following a 300,000-barrel draw. The estimate does not resolve the overseas supply constraint, and the official Energy Information Administration figures remain the more comprehensive test, but such a large build can temper the inference that every part of the oil market is becoming equally scarce.

The day’s macro releases also argued against treating the Treasury move as a simple response to accelerating growth. ADP’s weekly estimate improved by 4,000 to 16,250, supporting the view that private labor demand was still expanding. The Empire State index, however, dropped 13 points to 7.60 and undershot both the 14.75 consensus and the 14 forecast. It remained above zero, but the decline weakened the case that manufacturing momentum was strengthening into the Fed meeting.

Redbook same-store sales rose 8.5% from a year earlier in the week through Sept. 12, after 8.3%, indicating firm nominal spending at a subset of retailers. The measure is narrower than the government’s retail-sales report and does not separate volumes from prices. It therefore added evidence of current-dollar consumption without resolving whether households were purchasing more goods or paying more for them.

The 6-week bill auction cleared at 3.850%, up from 3.740% previously. That result was consistent with the higher expected policy rate, but without coverage or allotment information it did not establish the strength of demand. The bill move also lacked the funding-stress characteristics that would justify treating it as a conflict with the coupon curve.

Positioning increased the chance that the Fed decision would produce an abrupt move even if the policy outcome itself matched expectations. JPMorgan’s Treasury client survey showed short positions increasing by 10 percentage points in the week through Sept. 14, the fastest rise since early 2025, while neutral positions fell by 8 points. Futures open interest also showed bearish positions added before and after the stronger-than-expected inflation report. Bank of America described shorts as widespread across the curve, with little evidence that asset managers were buying the decline.

That bearishness is tactically important because it can amplify either direction. A message implying more than the roughly 50 basis points of tightening already priced for the rest of the year would validate the short base. A well-telegraphed quarter-point increase accompanied by credible but limited guidance could instead encourage profit-taking, particularly with the 10-year near 5% and positioning already stretched.

The market was much less prepared for a hold. Swaps put about 23 basis points of a 25-basis-point increase into Wednesday’s decision. Since 2008, the Fed has delivered a hike whenever expectations were this high, and Deutsche Bank estimated that an unchanged decision would constitute the largest dovish surprise at a scheduled meeting since the central bank began announcing decisions immediately after meetings in 1994. A hold could lower policy-sensitive short yields while lifting the long end if investors concluded that officials were tolerating too much inflation risk.

Equities reflected the pressure from both the discount rate and energy. More than 350 S&P 500 members declined, and the Dow lost about 1%. The broader S&P and Nasdaq posted smaller losses, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 0.40% after heavy weakness during the preceding week. The equity reaction was therefore broad but not indiscriminate. Higher Treasury yields made cash flows further in the future less valuable, while oil added a direct cost to consumers and corporate margins.

Bitcoin supplied a sharper example of risk sensitivity. It fell as much as 5.3% to $74,910 after the U.S. Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act, which needed 60 votes but failed 49-50. Ether dropped more than 8% intraday, and almost $300 million of bullish crypto positions were liquidated in the final hour before the vote. The legislative defeat was the immediate catalyst, but the decline was intensified by anxiety over higher rates and tighter liquidity.

## Japan and India Add Domestic Supply Shocks to the Global Selloff

Japan’s bond decline combined an international rise in yields with a new domestic fiscal question. The 10-year Japanese government-bond yield increased 4.5 basis points to 3.03%, its highest since 1996, after reports that officials were considering raising the country’s medium-term defense-spending target to as much as 3.5% of GDP. A lower goal of 3% was also under consideration, and no formal commitment had been made.

The scale of the possible change was large relative to Japan’s recent budget. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government accelerated defense-related spending to almost 2% of GDP in the fiscal year ended in March, two years ahead of schedule. On the Cabinet Office’s forecast for nominal GDP, however, the current fiscal year’s ¥10.6 trillion of defense and related spending amounts to about 1.5%. A 3.5% allocation on that basis would be roughly ¥24 trillion, more than twice the present sum.

Financing remained undefined. The Defense Ministry requested a record ¥8.9 trillion for the fiscal year beginning next April, 0.9% more than the current year, but many items in the request had not yet been assigned a cost. A new five-year defense plan is expected by year-end. Officials have signaled to U.S. counterparts that Japan is prepared to increase spending, while publicly maintaining that requirements should be determined by military needs rather than a predetermined monetary target.

The report overwhelmed a constructive 20-year JGB auction. The sale drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 4.01, above 3.98 previously and the 12-month average of 3.73. The auction tail narrowed to 0.15 from 0.17, and buying was spread across domestic lenders. Those results showed demand for long Japanese duration at the offered yield, but they could not settle the larger question of how much additional debt a defense expansion would require.

The Bank of Japan decision on Friday added another reason for investors to limit duration exposure. A rate increase was widely expected, leaving Governor Kazuo Ueda’s guidance on the pace and scope of further tightening as the larger variable. Higher policy rates, a weak yen and a possible fiscal expansion were all pushing in the same direction for JGB yields, even though a credible tightening path could eventually constrain inflation expectations.

India’s selloff was more directly tied to a known balance-sheet operation becoming a realized market event. After Monday’s holiday, 5-year government yields jumped as much as 22 basis points, the largest increase since May 2022, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose 8 basis points. The concentration in shorter maturities reflected the Reserve Bank of India’s plan to sell 1 trillion rupees of bonds, much of it in securities maturing in three to six years.

The RBI is seeking to remove surplus cash that it regards as an inflation risk. Outright sales create a more durable liquidity drain than temporary reverse-repurchase operations, but they also add tradable supply to a market already facing close to 8 trillion rupees of federal borrowing over the next six months and typically heavy issuance by Indian states. The central bank has capacity to continue: its sovereign-bond holdings increased more than 40% in the previous fiscal year to about 23 trillion rupees, or roughly 18% of outstanding central-government securities.

Oil intensified the pressure. India imports most of its crude, so prices above $100 worsen inflation, the current account and the fiscal burden associated with energy. August inflation had already moved closer to the top of the RBI’s 2%-6% target band. Kotak Mahindra economist Upasna Bhardwaj expected 50-75 basis points of rate increases and judged an October move substantially more likely.

The rupee weakened as the bond market reopened, and the RBI intervened to support the currency. That response did not remove the trade-off. Selling dollars can reduce currency pressure but also withdraw rupee liquidity; selling bonds drains cash more explicitly while exposing the short and intermediate curve to extra supply. The resulting flattening differs from the U.S. session’s small daily steepening because the RBI’s operation is aimed directly at the three-to-six-year sector.

## China’s Factory Resilience Fails to Reach Domestic Demand

China’s August data revealed an economy increasingly dependent on industrial production and exports while consumption, investment and property remained weak. Retail sales rose only 0.4% from a year earlier, below the 0.8% consensus and slower than July’s 0.6%. Fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% during the first eight months from a year earlier, slightly worse than expected, and property investment contracted 19.9%.

The labor market also softened. The urban unemployment rate increased unexpectedly to 5.3% from 5.2%. Auto sales fell 18.5% from a year earlier after the withdrawal of purchase subsidies weighed on demand. Excluding vehicles, retail sales grew 2.5%, matching July’s pace, which showed that the weakness was not uniform but remained severe in an important discretionary category.

Industrial output supplied the principal offset. Production increased 5.2% from a year earlier, exceeding expectations and accelerating from 4.5% in July. Export demand linked to the global buildout of artificial-intelligence infrastructure supported integrated circuits and other high-technology products. Capital spending on information transmission rose 28.4% in January through August, up from 26% over the first seven months, as projects under the government’s Six Networks program advanced.

The result was a sharper split between external production and domestic income. Strong exports can support the headline growth rate, but they have not yet produced enough household confidence or business investment to revive internal demand. Manufacturers’ average profit margin was 4.9% in July, better than a year earlier but still below the 6.7% reached in 2021. Falling property values and a worsening job market continued to restrain consumers.

Barclays, Oxford Economics and Macquarie estimated that third-quarter GDP was tracking about 4.3% growth from a year earlier based on the July and August data. That would place expansion at risk of falling below the official 4.5%-5% target range for a second consecutive quarter. The risk is that export strength gives policymakers reason to delay broader countercyclical support even as domestic demand deteriorates.

Policy expectations remained measured. The likely near-term response was faster deployment of already approved budget allocations rather than a major new stimulus package. An overhaul intended to reduce developers’ reliance on the property pre-sale model could protect homebuyers, but by delaying developers’ access to mortgage proceeds it may further reduce construction appetite and weaken local-government finances.

Chinese markets treated the release as a confirmation of an existing low-growth regime rather than an immediate policy shock. The yuan was steady in both onshore and offshore trading, and the 10-year government-bond yield was little changed at 1.68%. That stability contrasted with the selloffs in U.S., Japanese and Indian debt and helped explain the relative strength of Asian high-yield issuers with access to inexpensive local-currency funding.

## Credit Stays Open as Issuer-Level Distress Becomes More Visible

Broad U.S. credit remained orderly despite the rise in Treasury yields. Investment-grade spreads tightened modestly, while high-yield spreads widened only modestly. The divergence between LQD’s near-flat total return and losses of about 0.20% in HYG and JNK suggested that the market was distinguishing duration pressure from incremental lower-quality risk rather than moving into a generalized liquidation.

The underlying financing picture was more complex. KKR said it structured or syndicated more than $80 billion of private investment-grade transactions in the first half of 2026 and by Sept. 1 had doubled the amount originated during all of 2025. Insurance capital anchored many of the deals. Borrowers increasingly used special-purpose vehicles to finance assets off balance sheet, preserving corporate ratings while raising cash for investment.

Artificial intelligence is an important source of that demand. KKR estimated that AI infrastructure could require $7.6 trillion of capital spending over the next five years, an amount likely to exceed the capacity of traditional balance sheets and public bond markets alone. The firm raised $15 billion of third-party credit capital this year, 29% more than in the same period of 2025, and managed $139 billion in private credit within $293 billion of total credit assets.

The growth of private investment-grade finance does not eliminate project risk. Carlyle’s Jason Thomas warned that some data-center lending relies heavily on the investment-grade standing of the sponsor rather than an independent judgment of the underlying project’s revenue. He compared the structure with the pre-financial-crisis assumption that banks could absorb mortgage exposures if needed. Thomas emphasized that current investment-grade sponsors were not in that position, but said rising liabilities and a widening range of potential data-center outcomes could eventually weaken that support.

The underwriting question is becoming more important as risk premiums compress. If lenders treat the sponsor’s balance sheet as the principal protection, rapidly expanding commitments can make each additional project less insulated from the operating performance of the facilities themselves. That concern sits beside the more conventional risks of tenant concentration, power availability, changing computing technology and the timing of AI revenue.

Brightshore Capital entered another area where higher rates are creating private-credit opportunities. The real-estate manager launched a $250 million debt platform focused on stretch-senior loans, mezzanine finance, preferred equity and B-notes. By selling senior portions of transactions, Brightshore said the capital could support more than $1 billion of deals.

Homebuilders and residential developers are confronting elevated construction costs, a wall of maturities and refinancing rates far above those available when projects began. Oversupplied markets such as Austin are especially vulnerable where lower rents and higher operating costs meet construction loans coming due. The platform’s launch showed how private capital is moving toward the refinancing gap even as those same conditions raise the risk of weaker collateral performance.

Issuer-specific losses demonstrated the other side of that opportunity. Zorlu Enerji’s 2030 dollar bond fell as much as 11 points to about 63 cents, its largest decline on record, after the Turkish energy company hired Houlihan Lokey and Servo Capital as debt advisers. The appointment came two months after Vestel Elektronik, another Zorlu Group company, retained Houlihan for restructuring discussions, raising concern that financial stress was spreading across the conglomerate.

Zorlu Enerji’s first-half revenue fell to 13 billion lira from 17.3 billion a year earlier. The lira had weakened about 15% against the dollar over 12 months, increasing the local-currency burden of its international debt, while net debt stood at $1.25 billion at midyear. The company issued its debut $1 billion international bond in 2024. Its advisers had only just been appointed, so the market decline reflected uncertainty over a process rather than agreed restructuring terms.

Biscuit International’s loans were also moving deeper into distress only three months after the company completed a liability-management transaction. Management told creditors that second-quarter and early-summer performance was weak as sales volumes declined and agricultural and ingredient costs increased. Raw-material hedges were not expected to offset the full pressure because competition limited the company’s ability to pass on costs.

The June transaction extended term loans and a revolving facility, subordinated €130 million of notes and changed payment terms on a €150 million second-lien loan. Those measures provided more time, but Moody’s continued to view the capital structure as unsustainable and liquidity as weak. High working-capital requirements mean that an extension alone cannot resolve the credit if operating cash flow keeps deteriorating.

Asian high-yield debt provided a contrasting regional picture. Dollar-denominated Asian junk bonds had returned 4.3% for the year, compared with 1.8% for U.S. counterparts, and their yield premiums reached a record low in the preceding week. A Moody’s study counted 43 corporate issuer defaults in the U.S. through July and 20 in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, but only one in Asia-Pacific among the companies it rated.

Cheaper domestic funding in China and faster regional growth have supported issuer fundamentals. Even lower-rated Chinese companies could borrow in local currency for shorter maturities at around 1.7%. Asia ex-Japan nonfinancial high-yield issuance in dollars rose 20% from a year earlier to about $12 billion, still far below more than $220 billion in U.S. high-yield issuance.

The outperformance carries its own valuation risk. Asian high-yield notes lost 0.4% in September through the reporting date, while Chinese junk bonds gained 0.2%. A Fed increase and higher U.S. yields can pressure Asian central banks outside China to tighten or defend currencies, raising local funding costs. Issuance is also beginning to recover from the depressed levels that followed the collapse of China’s property-bond market, which once sold more than $50 billion of high-yield notes annually.

Gabon was an example of country-specific improvement overriding the broader emerging-market decline. Its dollar bonds rallied after a government audit put consolidated debt at $16.7 billion, almost one-fifth below the initial estimate. The revised stock equaled 69% of GDP. Bonds due in February 2031 rose 1.36 cents to 87.84 cents on the dollar, making Gabon’s three international notes the best performers in emerging markets during the session.

The audit reduced the recognized total from almost 11.7 trillion CFA francs to 9.5 trillion at the end of 2025 after reviewing obligations related to unexecuted projects, funds that did not reach Treasury accounts and other commitments. The government submitted the findings to the International Monetary Fund and plans to use them in negotiations over a new program, arrears settlement and a sustainable debt strategy. The lower total improves the starting position, but the country still must agree on how verified obligations will be paid and prevent new arrears.

Indonesia offered a more qualified improvement in sovereign credibility. President Prabowo Subianto replaced Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa with Suahasil Nazara, a former deputy finance minister familiar to markets. The move followed a leadership change at Bank Indonesia and was interpreted as an effort to stabilize institutions after policy volatility contributed to about $1.9 billion of capital outflows this year.

Nazara pledged prudence and a deficit below the legal ceiling of 3% of GDP. Investors still want evidence that he can protect fiscal discipline while financing the president’s social programs and growth plans and clarifying the role of sovereign wealth fund Danantara. Indonesian local bonds had received foreign inflows for four consecutive months and the rupiah had recovered about 3% from its June low, but Tuesday’s currency decline showed that personnel changes had not eliminated sensitivity to oil and global rates.

## Europe’s Rate Pricing Runs Ahead of Central-Bank Guidance

European money markets continued to price a more aggressive response to the energy shock than central bankers had endorsed. Swaps implied four additional quarter-point increases from the European Central Bank over the next 12 months and five from the Bank of England. Natural gas had returned to levels last seen in 2022, while oil moved above $108, lifting short-dated yields and expected rate volatility.

The ECB had already increased rates twice since the Iran conflict began, most recently taking its deposit rate to the upper end of estimates of neutral. Officials declined to commit to a fixed sequence. President Christine Lagarde acknowledged that inflation would remain elevated as the energy shock lasted longer than anticipated, but the market path would take policy well into restrictive territory.

The BOE’s communication gap was even wider. Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden had said he was comfortable with current policy while acknowledging upside risks. No change was expected at Thursday’s meeting, although swaps assigned a 30% probability to an immediate increase. With no press conference after the decision, the wording of the statement will have to address both the inflation shock and the market’s expectation of five moves.

Balance-sheet policy could provide a separate adjustment. Officials at the BOE, Treasury and Debt Management Office were reported to have drafted plans that could end active sales of long-dated gilts, though the Monetary Policy Committee had not made a final decision. Markets expected total annual balance-sheet runoff to slow to £50 billion from October. Maintaining the present sales mix at that pace would imply only about £4 billion of long-dated active sales because maturities beyond the intermediate sector account for roughly 20% of the current program.

Stopping those sales would reduce one source of prospective long-duration supply without reversing quantitative tightening. The distinction is important with the 30-year gilt yield near 5.9% and the central bank carrying large losses on bonds bought after the financial crisis and pandemic. It would address market capacity rather than substitute for the policy-rate decision.

France’s officials sought to reassure investors that rising yields had not impaired government access. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the Treasury had completed 85% of its annual issuance program, while Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said bids continued to exceed the securities offered. The French 10-year spread over Germany nevertheless traded around 97 basis points after reaching levels not seen since the euro-area debt crisis.

The pressure reflected more than the global selloff. France faces a large deficit, weak growth and a presidential election in seven months. Higher energy costs and heavier international issuance compound those domestic risks. Moulin argued that central-bank credibility was essential because part of the rise in yields came from inflation expectations, while also pointing to the global competition for capital created by U.S. technology borrowing.

Investors were increasingly differentiating among European sovereigns rather than treating the core as uniformly safer. Bulgaria’s 10-year bond yielded 4.40%, nearly 90 basis points more than Germany despite public debt of about 30% of GDP. Latvia and Lithuania were the year’s strongest-performing euro-denominated sovereign markets, while France and Belgium had lost around 3%.

Hungary also attracted demand after an election ended 16 years of rule under Viktor Orban and the new government set a goal of euro adoption by 2030. That plan includes reducing the deficit to 3% of GDP from an expected 7.5%. Foreign holdings of Hungarian bonds and bills reached a record in July. The opportunity remains accompanied by currency, liquidity and energy risks, but the shift shows how fiscal direction can matter more than conventional geographic labels when benchmark yields are rising across the region.

## Forward Market Significance

The Federal Reserve’s Sept. 16 decision, economic projections and Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference are the central test for a Treasury market already positioned heavily for higher yields. The target range is currently 3.5%-3.75%, and markets overwhelmingly expect a quarter-point increase. The immediate question is not only whether the Fed delivers, but whether the projections and Warsh’s language validate roughly 50 basis points of tightening through year-end.

A hold would be the larger market surprise and could produce a curve split: shorter yields would likely lose some expected policy premium, while long yields could rise if investors questioned the Fed’s inflation response. A quarter-point increase accompanied by unusually patient guidance presents a milder version of the same risk. A forceful message about further action would support the front-end repricing but could lift real yields and deepen the pressure on equities, housing and duration-sensitive credit.

Tuesday’s data leave room for both sides of that debate. ADP’s weekly employment estimate improved to 16,250, but the Empire State index fell to 7.60, far below consensus. The Fed must decide how much weight to place on resilient hiring and nominal spending against evidence that manufacturing momentum is slowing.

August retail sales and import and export prices arrive before the policy announcement. Headline retail sales are expected to rise 0.8% after a 0.6% decline. Import prices are expected to increase 0.4% after falling 0.4%, while export prices are expected to rise 0.5% after a 1.3% decline. The combination will show whether household demand is rebounding as external cost pressure increases. The NY Fed services index, business inventories and the NAHB housing index will add narrower readings on activity and rate sensitivity.

Oil remains capable of changing that interpretation. The official EIA inventory report follows the API estimate of a 7.14 million-barrel crude build. A similarly large official increase would provide some domestic cushion against the international supply shock. The more consequential physical questions are whether Saudi Arabia restores the East-West pipeline, whether delayed European cargoes are delivered and whether Libyan production returns. Inventory accumulation in the U.S. cannot fully offset a prolonged impairment of Middle Eastern export capacity.

The Sept. 17 labor and regional-manufacturing data will test whether the Empire State decline was isolated. Initial jobless claims are expected at 208,000 after 206,000, and continuing claims at 1.78 million after 1.774 million. The Philadelphia Fed index is expected to fall to 30.5 from 47.4. Its employment, new-orders, capital-spending and prices-paid components will indicate whether activity is slowing broadly or remaining firm while cost pressure persists.

Treasury supply returns with the Sept. 17 10-year TIPS auction after a previous result of 2.438%. The market’s 10-year real yield is now 2.62%, up more than 20 basis points in a week. The sale will test demand for inflation-protected duration after the nominal 20-year auction cleared at a higher yield and the broader Treasury market closed with the 10-year above 5%.

The BOE decision on Sept. 17 has two independent dimensions. Markets expect the policy rate to remain unchanged but assign a meaningful probability to an increase as energy prices rise. The statement must also explain the next annual quantitative-tightening plan. Confirmation that the Bank will slow runoff and end active sales of long-dated gilts would reduce supply pressure at the far end without resolving the inflation question.

The BOJ follows on Sept. 18. An increase is widely expected, so Ueda’s guidance will carry more market information than the first step. A signal of continued tightening would support the yen but could keep JGB yields elevated and encourage Japanese institutions to retain more funds domestically. The unresolved defense-spending proposal creates a separate fiscal test: investors need the final target, implementation period and funding source before judging how much additional issuance it requires.

India’s next test is the execution of the RBI’s bond sales. The first tranche targets securities concentrated in the short and intermediate sector. Tuesday’s 22-basis-point rise in the 5-year yield showed how sensitive that part of the curve is to outright liquidity withdrawal. Auction cutoffs and the behavior of the rupee will indicate whether the adjustment remains localized or becomes a broader tightening of financial conditions.

China’s policy response will be watched through late September. Industrial output remains strong enough to discourage an immediate large stimulus, but 0.4% retail-sales growth, a 7.2% investment contraction and a 19.9% property-investment decline increase the cost of delay. Faster deployment of existing fiscal allocations would support infrastructure and production; a broader response would require evidence that officials are prepared to address household income and property weakness rather than rely predominantly on exports.

Credit markets face execution rather than a single aggregate test. Zorlu Enerji’s advisers must clarify whether their work concerns refinancing, asset sales or a broader restructuring. Biscuit International must demonstrate that its June maturity extension can withstand continued operating weakness and working-capital pressure. Private lenders financing AI and real estate will be judged on whether sponsor support and collateral cash flows remain credible as liabilities grow.

Gabon’s revised debt stock must be converted into an agreement with the IMF and other financial partners. The audit improved the recognized balance-sheet position and triggered an immediate bond rally, but the next stage requires a plan for verified arrears and future borrowing. Indonesia’s Nazara faces a similar credibility test through the 2027 budget: keeping the deficit below 3% of GDP while funding the government’s agenda would give investors more evidence than the cabinet change alone.

Across those events, the market is not confronting an absence of capital. Treasury auctions, private investment-grade transactions and selected emerging-market credits continue to attract buyers. The immediate constraint is price: governments and companies can still borrow, but the required real yield, contractual protection and sponsor support are rising as oil, monetary tightening and competing demands for long-term financing converge.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
The 10-year Treasury yield ended at 5.003%, up 1.5 basis points, after reaching 5.04%, while the 30-year rose 2.2 basis points to 5.368%. Smaller increases in the 2-year and 5-year yields produced modest curve steepening as the $13 billion 20-year auction cleared at 5.420%, its highest yield since the tenor was reintroduced.

The move came principally through real yields: the 10-year real yield rose 1.3 basis points to 2.62%, while the breakeven increased only 0.2 basis point to 2.383%. Oil intensified the inflation risk as disruptions in Saudi Arabia and Libya lifted WTI 3.93% and Brent 2.48%, but the limited breakeven response indicated that tighter policy, heavy financing needs and the required real return on duration remained the larger forces in Treasury pricing.

U.S. data were mixed, with ADP employment improving while the Empire State manufacturing index fell well below consensus. Markets still assigned about a 94% probability to a quarter-point Fed increase and priced roughly 50 basis points of tightening through year-end. Risk assets weakened without generalized funding stress, while Japan and India experienced sharper bond selloffs tied to domestic fiscal and liquidity-supply concerns.
